title: SLO downgrade choreography and customer communication runbook
author: Maya Kline
content:
Summary

Purpose: This runbook defines the operational choreography, decision matrix, and pre-approved customer communication templates for performing a controlled SLO downgrade (temporary degradation of SLO targets or feature gating) during acute capacity pressure or persistent regressions. It is intended for oncall SREs, service owners, and support/CS leads who must coordinate fast, safe, and auditable degradations while minimizing customer impact and billing risk.

Scope
- Applies to Redwood-hosted inference services and shared model-serving clusters (both hosted and Dedicated managed nodes).
- Not intended for proactive permanent SLO changes (those go through SLO governance). Use this runbook for emergency, temporary downgrades and scheduled, time-boxed degradations with rollback criteria.

Owner and contacts
- Runbook owner: eng-sre (page steward: Maya Kline)
- Primary oncall channel: #oncall-inference (Slack)
- Pager duty escalation: SRE Primary -> SRE Secondary -> SRE Guild Lead (escalation rows in PagerDuty)
- Support/CS notify: cs-notify@redwood.com (automated)

Definitions and safe terms
- SLO downgrade: temporary change to the operational target (e.g., target p99 latency from 300ms -> 600ms for up to 4 hours, or lowering availability target 99.95% -> 99.5%).
- Degradation window: duration the downgrade is authorized for (max default 4 hours without exec approval).
- Capacity hedge: short-term reserved capacity allocation to reduce downgrade scope (e.g., burst GPUs, preemptible pools).
- Burn-rate trigger: 3x baseline for 15 minutes (example) meaning error budget consumption or latency SLI burn above this triggers immediate review.

Pre-approve policy (quick reference)
1) Minor downgrades (non-customer-facing feature quality changes, non-critical customers): oncall SRE + service owner signoff in Slack — allowed up to 2 hours.
2) Moderate downgrades (observable customer impact for non-enterprise tenants): oncall SRE + service owner + product PM approval — allowed up to 4 hours.
3) Major downgrades (billing-affecting or impacting enterprise-tier customers): Exec-level approval (SRE Director or VP Product) required — allowed up to 8 hours; CS outreach mandatory.

Decision matrix
| Trigger condition | Immediate action | Downgrade class | Approver(s) | Max window |
|---|---:|---|---|---:|
| Sudden p99 latency > 3x baseline for 15m | Open incident, notify service owner | Minor | Oncall SRE + service owner | 2h |
| Rolling errors across 10% of hosts > 10m | Open incident, isolate host pool, consider downgrade | Moderate | Oncall SRE + PM | 4h |
| Sustained >50% error budget burn in 1h | Emergency call, CS standby | Major | Exec + CS lead | 8h |

Runbook: step-by-step choreography (execute in this order)
1) Triage and evidence collection (0–10 min)
   - Confirm SLI failure: check dashboards (Dash ID: inference-slo-ops-001) and alert details.
   - Snapshot telemetry: run CLI snippet to capture recent traces and token-level telemetry:
     - curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $RD_TOKEN" "https://ops.redwood/api/v1/telemetry/snapshot?service=inference&window=30m" > /tmp/evidence.json
   - Create incident and link snapshot (Jira: INF-INC-<timestamp>).
2) Rapid mitigation attempts (10–30 min)
   - Apply capacity hedge: trigger capacity pipeline: 
     - rwctl capacity reserve --pool burst-gpu --tokens 2 --reason "emergency hedge"
   - Toggle non-essential features: route feature-flagged heavy prompts to degraded pipeline (feature flag id: ff/inference-long-context-degrade).
   - If mitigations restore SLIs within 10 minutes, close the incident with remediation notes.
3) Decide downgrade (30–60 min)
   - If mitigations fail and decision matrix indicates downgrade, perform pre-approval flow per policy above. Record approvals in incident timeline.
4) Execute graceful downgrade (explicit commands and checks)
   - Prepare: open a coordinated Slack thread in #oncall-inference and tag @service-owner, @pm, @cs-lead.
   - Apply downgrade configuration (examples):
     - Increase p99 latency SLO ceiling: rwctl slo update --service inference --slo p99_latency --target_ms 600 --reason "emergency downgrade - high tail latency"
     - For availability: rwctl slo update --service inference --slo availability --target_pct 99.5 --duration 4h --reason "emergency capacity shortage"
   - Enable progressive gating: set low-priority tenant throttle to 20% to preserve enterprise lanes:
     - rwctl throttle set --service inference --priority low --rate 0.8 --duration 4h
   - Verify: monitor SLI dashboard and confirm reduced burn-rate within 5–10 min.
5) Customer communication (simultaneous with execution)
   - CS outreach: CS lead composes targeted messages using pre-approved templates (see below). For enterprise customers, open a priority ticket and assign a CS rep.
   - Public status page: if user-visible degradation expected >10 minutes, update status.redwood.com with short entry: "Investigating increased latency for inference API; temporary performance reduction in effect. Full details and ETA in linked incident."
6) Observe and hold (while downgrade active)
   - Runbook owner or oncall checks every 15 minutes and records telemetry snapshots.
   - If SLI trend stabilizes and error budget burn < 1.5x baseline for 30 minutes, begin rollback per rollback criteria.
7) Rollback and retrospective (post-downgrade)
   - Rollback command examples:
     - rwctl slo rollback --service inference --to-version stable-2027-11-01 --reason "post-mitigation rollback"
     - rwctl throttle reset --service inference --priority low
   - Close incident only when SLIs returned to pre-incident baseline for 60 minutes.
   - Run a 72-hour post-incident action plan: include capacity remediation, root cause analysis, and SLO governance request if permanent SLO change needed.

Customer messaging templates (pre-approved)
- Short customer-facing status update (status page / public):
  "We are experiencing degraded performance on the Redwood inference API. We have applied a temporary, controlled performance profile to maintain overall availability while we investigate. There is no expected data exposure; we will provide updates every 30 minutes."

- Enterprise SLA notification (email / ticket):
  Subject: Redwood Inference — Temporary performance mitigation in effect
  Body: Dear <Customer>
  We are currently managing an operational event that affects p99 latency for inference calls. To maintain availability for all tenants we have applied a temporary performance profile for up to <window>. Our CS team (assigned: <name>) is available for direct questions. We expect to restore normal performance within <ETA>. Incident link: <Jira link>.

- Refund/credit policy note (pre-approved language):
  "If the event results in a prolonged SLA breach beyond the authorized degrade window, credits will be handled per contractual terms. Immediate credits are not issued without post-incident verification."

Telemetry and tooling checklist (must be executed when downgrading)
- Dashboards to snapshot: inference-slo-ops-001, token-latency-quantiles-002, model-kvcache-hitrate-003.
- Alerts to mute during downgrade (to prevent noise): slo-alerts/p99-spike; errorbudget-rapidburn. Document muted alerts in incident.
- Evidence artifacts: telemetry snapshot files, rwctl audit logs (~/var/log/rwctl/audit.log), Slack approval thread permalink.

Safety and rollback criteria (must be met before full rollback)
- SLI p99 below 2x baseline for 60 minutes OR error budget burn < 1.2x baseline for 30 minutes.
- No new host-level OOMs or host restarts in the last 20 minutes.
- All throttled/affected tenants show request success rate >= 99% for 30 minutes.

Post-incident actions and tickets (template tasks)
1) RCA: owner assigned within 24 hours, RCA draft due in 72 hours.
2) Capacity remediation: estimate hours and cost for burst hedges; submit capacity request to infra-planning board.
3) SLO governance request: if downgrade indicates recurring capacity constraint, open an SLO governance proposal to consider permanent changes.
4) Runbook edits: update decision thresholds and sample commands based on lessons learned.

Appendix: quick command references
- Reserve capacity: rwctl capacity reserve --pool <name> --tokens <n> --duration <m>
- Apply SLO change: rwctl slo update --service <svc> --slo <name> --target_ms|pct <value> --duration <m>
- Snapshot telemetry: rwctl telemetry snapshot --service <svc> --window 30m --out /tmp/snap.json
- Rollback SLO: rwctl slo rollback --service <svc> --to-version <tag>

References
